content:
ryan: FYI nightly runs started spiking NaN errors in the positional-encoding path (ROPE) after the kernel-selector change landed.
ryan: Repro is small but deterministic on long sequences (>8k). dumping a quick repro below.
ryan: ```python
# repro against local runtime image: registry.redwood/runtime:canary-8f3b
from runtime_client import RuntimeClient
c = RuntimeClient(url=\"http://localhost:8080\")
input = \"A\" * 9000
r = c.generate(model=\"gpt-lite-rope\", prompt=input, max_tokens=1)
print(r[\"tokens\"])  # sometimes contains NaN / inf
```
deepa: ugh. saw similar in my tests but assumed it was our quant path. good catch.
deepa: can you paste the failing stacktrace from the runner logs?
ryan: log snippet:
ryan: ```
E 2025-11-18T02:12:45Z kernel_run.cpp:254 kernel_run: accum value overflow -> NaN at head 12, layer 23
E 2025-11-18T02:12:45Z runtime.cpp:411 Runtime::step: exception: NaN detected in attention accum
```
marta: which commit in selector? I reverted the low-latency branch yesterday in us-east but not canary.
ryan: selector commit is 8f3b2a7 - it changes kernel choice heuristics to prefer fused-rotary kernels for >4096 tokens.
linh: hypothesis: fused-rotary uses different accumulate summation order and triggers underflow/overflow with bf16->fp32 path.
linh: quick idea: add an eps clamp before the final divide and see if repro disappears.
josh: can we run a focused unit test with randomized sequence lengths to catch this in CI? I can add one to eng-runtime/tests/posenc_repro.py
deepa: also want a perf-safe fallback: if the fused kernel reports any non-finite, fallback to reference kernel for that request. low cost to implement and avoids user impact.
marta: agree. hold canary in prod until we have a patch. @infra-bot please hold rollout in us-west-2 and us-east-1 canaries.
infra-bot: deploy: Rollout hold placed by marta on deployment/runtime-canary in: us-west-2, us-east-1
ryan: quick patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456
ryan: patch adds: 1) eps clamp in fused kernel 2) non-finite detection + per-request fallback 3) test reproducer
josh: running the repro against r1456 locally now.
josh: good news: with the fallback enabled the request completes and matches reference output for 10/10 runs. no NaNs.
linh: would like to avoid perf cliff for the fallback path — maybe only enable fallback when fused kernel returns non-finite, not preemptively.
marta: agreed. also add telemetry: increment metric runtime.kernel.fallback.count with reason=nonfinite and runtime.kernel.fused.nan_detected boolean.
deepa: add a postmortem task: confirm whether quantized kernels have same issue (cc @josh)
ryan: I'll backport hotfix to 8f3b branch and submit a patch to the selector to avoid choosing fused-rotary for sequences that historically triggered issues.
marta: timeline: backport + canary redeploy with fallback on by default for canary yesterday + metric observed -> decide broad rollout.
linh: note for RFC follow-up: we should define kernel API contract for "safety checks" (finite checks, saturation reporting) so selectors can be simpler.
ryan: opening a follow-up RFC draft: https://redwood-internal/notes/rfc/kernel-safety-checks (WIP)
marta: thanks. great triage. keep updates short here, but please add all test logs to the PR.
ryan: will do. tagging this as high priority. :thumbsup:
